faq.q: What is the new tax regime and is it mandatory?
faq.a: The new tax regime, which offers lower tax rates without most deductions, is now the default option. However, you still have the choice to opt for the old tax regime if you prefer to claim various deductions like Section 80C, HRA, etc.

faq.q: What is the tax-free income limit under the new tax regime for FY 2025-26?
faq.a: Under the new tax regime for FY 2025-26, income up to ₹12 lakh can be effectively tax-free for resident individuals due to an enhanced rebate under Section 87A. For salaried individuals, with a standard deduction of ₹75,000, the effective tax-free income can go up to ₹12.75 lakh.

faq.q: What are Form 26AS and AIS, and why are they important?
faq.a: Form 26AS is your tax credit statement, showing all taxes deducted (TDS) or collected (TCS) against your PAN. The Annual Information Statement (AIS) and Taxpayer Information Summary (TIS) provide a more comprehensive view of your financial transactions, including interest, dividends, and mutual fund transactions. It's crucial to cross-check these with your ITR to ensure accuracy and avoid discrepancies.

faq.q: Can I revise my ITR if I make a mistake?
faq.a: Yes, if you discover an error after filing your original ITR, you can file a "revised return" up to March 31, 2027, for AY 2026-27.

faq.q: What if I have income from futures and options (F&O) trading?
faq.a: For AY 2026-27, the ITR forms require specific reporting of turnover and income from futures and options (F&O) trading. Ensure you accurately disclose these details.
